- contractual flow-down for data processing/security obligations (DPA clauses)
- a notice-and-consent path for additions (30 days for notice + approval exception for low-risk infra)
- evidence for SOC2-type controls where data access is possible

Ben —

Thanks for sending the redline. I've reviewed section 8.3 and the proposed flow-down language. A couple of notes from Cloudline legal: we are generally comfortable with flow-downs but need clarity on two operational points before sign-off:

1) Downstream vendor list: we can provide a current list but want to reserve the right to add routine cloud infra vendors (IaaS, CDN) without separate approval. Would Redwood accept a carve-out for core infra providers if they have independent certifications?

2) Audit assistance: Cloudline prefers audit-by-exception (i.e., we provide SOC2 reports; in rare cases where Redwood requests on-site evidence we require a narrow scope and 90 days' notice).

I've attached a very small mark-up of the MSA redline with our comments (see attachment). Would Redwood legal be open to an annex approach that references the DPA by hyperlink + an exhibit with the subprocessor list? That keeps the order form concise.

Proposed next step: call between legal teams Wednesday 5/13 10:00 PT to reconcile language. Please confirm.

Cheers,

Maya / Cloudline legal team —

Thanks for the quick review and the annotated PDF. A few Redwood legal positions to make the Wednesday call efficient: 

1) Infra carve-out: Redwood can accept a limited carve-out for large cloud providers (IaaS/PaaS) provided they are certified (SOC2/HIPAA as applicable) and the carve-out expressly excludes any service that processes customer content in cleartext (we will not carve-out logging vendors that can see customer payloads).

2) Audit assistance: audit-by-exception is acceptable. We will require a right to request evidence and an operational contact. The 90-day notice window is longer than typical; we ask to tighten to 45 days (with emergency exception).

3) Annex approach: good idea. We propose: 
- MSA references a DPA exhibit in the order form.
- DPA exhibit lists subprocessors and cites certificate/evidence buckets (SOC2 link or similar).
- For changes: Cloudline provides 30 days' notice for new subs; Redwood has a 10-business-day review window (short call to raise material objections).

I've attached a short counter-markup (Cloudline_MSA_Redline_20260512.docx) that implements these positions. Please review ahead of the call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
